Q1.  In the late 1800s, one whiskey brand dominated the global market. They were especially dismissive of their closest rivals, refusing to adopt a new invention that would change the industry forever. Then Prohibition wiped out their biggest overseas market, a war of independence cut off trade with their nearest neighbour, and the Great Depression finished them off. By the 1960s they had to merge with every surviving competitor just to stay alive.

Next
In 1955, one musician walked onstage holding a glass of whiskey and announced to the audience: "Ladies and gentlemen, this is the nectar of the gods." Within a year, sales of that whiskey had doubled. Demand outstripped supply so severely it delayed exports for nearly two decades. The musician was later buried with a bottle of it.
